references.text: Contrast between Benjamin's temporary victory (18,000 fallen) and their ultimate destruction (25,100 fallen), illustrating escalating judgment.
The specific loss in the source verse (18,000) is part of the total judgment against Benjamin (25,000) described here.
Direct numerical confirmation: both verses refer to the 18,000 fallen on the second day of battle.
Contrast between Benjamin's original strength (26,000) and the loss in one day (18,000), illustrating the scope of judgment.
Theological contrast: Benjamin's victory over a superior army (400,000) shows that human strength does not determine the outcome.
